text:
alex_w: Quick sanity check — ran apples-to-apples streaming vs non-streaming on the thin-chunk binary. Non-streaming p99 < streaming for long seqs (>=4k) but streaming wins around 1k-2k. wondering if kernel selection/batching heuristics are masking the behavior.

mira: Can you paste the harness config + any kernel map overrides you used? :thinking:

alex_w: Paste below. Replay harness w/ client pacing + variable chunk sizes. Forced one run to use an alternate kernel map (`aten_eviction`) to see effect.

```
mode: streaming
chunk_size: 64
client_readloop: continuous
batch_window_ms: 8
kernel_hint: auto
kv_cache: enabled
```

devon: Aten_eviction is going to punish streaming — more KV churn per chunk. Did you log KV hit-rate?

alex_w: Yep. KV hit-rate: streaming run 72% vs non-streaming 91% on same trace. Small chunks cause cache churn.

sanjay: That explains the p99 regression — extra host<->device round-trips. Any perf captures (flamegraph, nvprof, perf stat)?

alex_w: I collected nvprof + flamegraph. nvprof shows kernel launch overhead dominating for streaming when chunk < 128. Snippet:
```
KernelLaunchOverhead: 1.8ms avg
ForwardKernel(layers): 0.6ms avg
KVRead: 0.9ms avg (called ~15x per request)
```

mira: So a lot of micro launches + repeated KVRead calls. Two obvious levers: increase chunk_size or change batching heuristics to group chunk requests before dispatch.

devon: Also check client readloop behavior — client acks/flushing pattern may force server to push tiny partial batches. Server-side coalescing (wait X ms or until depth N) could help.

alex_w: I tried server-side batch-window = 12ms and it recovered most tail latency for streaming. Results:
- streaming chunk=64, no server-batch: p50 28ms, p99 450ms
- streaming chunk=64, server-batch=12ms: p50 32ms, p99 120ms
- non-streaming (single-shot): p50 25ms, p99 95ms

sanjay: Good. That implies kernel selector should prefer low-launch-overhead kernels when avg_chunk_len small. Suggest heuristic: if avg_chunk_len < 128 && qps > 100 then prefer fused-kernel variant.

mira: Agreed, but be cautious — fused kernels can have worse cold-starts. Also for streaming we should bias KV eviction to be sticky for recent prefixes to reduce churn.

devon: Action items: 
1) alex — PR for server-side batching opt (default 10ms for streaming) + perf tests.
2) mira — add telemetry: per-request KV hit-rate, kernel launch counts to Console.
3) sanjay — prototype kernel-selector rule based on avg_chunk_len.

alex_w: Filed perf run in CI: ci-bot started perf job 1808502468-streaming-proxy-readloop-thin-chunk-profiling (run id: perf-2026-03-18-09-14). I attached nvprof + flamegraph to the PR.

ci-bot: started perf job 1808502468-streaming-proxy-readloop-thin-chunk-profiling
ci-bot: run id: perf-2026-03-18-09-14

mira: One more ask — capture context-switch and syscall stats. nvprof doesn't show those and I suspect client readloop wakeups causing syscall churn.

alex_w: Perf stat excerpt:
```
cycles: 1.2e9
context-switches: 42k
syscalls: 9.8k
poll-wakeup-events: 18k
```

devon: 42k context switches is high — likely per-chunk socket wakeups. Server-side coalescing should reduce that a lot.

sanjay: Also double-check kernel_selector logging. If selector misses small seq length buckets we fall back to generic kernel with higher launch overhead. Add logging event when fallback occurs.

alex_w: Copy. I'll run another A/A tomorrow with server-batch=10ms + sticky KV policy + kernel-selector patch. Will upload artifacts.

mira: If the A/A shows parity we can flip streaming default to enable server-batching for thin-chunk traces.

devon: :thumbsup:

alex_w: Thanks all — updating the PR thread with artifacts and results.
